title: Understanding Multi-View Transformers
claim: Probing intermediate residual states of a feed-forward model reveals how its internal 3D geometry gradually emerges across layers.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, decoder blocks with probes feeding point-cloud renderings below
description: A single wide horizontal diagram reading left to right. Two photos of a red fire hydrant from different viewpoints feed into pink 'Shared Encoder' boxes, which are linked by a dotted line. The encoded features run into a series of gray decoder blocks labeled 0, 1, 3 and 11, with ellipses between them. Each block holds small colored modules: blue self-attention, orange cross-attention and green MLP. Curved skip-connection arrows loop around the modules. Yellow oval 'Probe' nodes hang below each module and attach with dashed arrows. Dotted lines fan out from the probes to 3D point-cloud renderings of the hydrant. The clouds go from noisy and fragmented at block 0 to coherent and dense at block 11. A pink 'Output head' oval sits at the end. The eye goes first to the hydrant point clouds and the yellow probes.
caption: Overview of our interpretability approach. We probe the skip connections of DUSt3R's multi-view transformer decoder for pointmaps and visualize the gradual development of DUSt3R's latent 3D geometry, correspondence, and camera pose estimate.
abstract: Multi-view transformers such as DUSt3R are revolutionizing 3D vision by solving 3D tasks in a feed-forward manner. However, contrary to previous optimization-based pipelines, the inner mechanisms of multi-view transformers are unclear. Their black-box nature makes further improvements beyond data scaling challenging and complicates usage in safety- and reliability-critical applications. Here, we present an approach for probing and visualizing 3D representations from the residual connections of the multi-view transformers' layers. In this manner, we investigate a variant of the DUSt3R model, shedding light on the development of its latent state across blocks, the role of the individual layers, and suggest how it differs from methods with stronger inductive biases of explicit global pose. Finally, we show that the investigated variant of DUSt3R estimates correspondences that are refined with reconstructed geometry. The code used for the analysis is available at https://github.com/JulienGaubil/und3rstand .
